# Paper Read Round (FAR / Premium Loops)

[← Amazon](../README.md) · [Every Amazon question](../../amazon.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/paper-read-round-far)

`deep-dive` `ml-knowledge` `presentation`

---

## Requirements

- Read the assigned paper completely and absorb its contents (a recent assignment, for example, was the DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report).
- Be prepared to examine the problem definition, central contribution, architecture, design reasoning, supporting evidence, weaknesses, and the path from research to production in detail.
- Expect 20–25 minutes of LP-style behavioral questions alongside the paper discussion.

## Examples

A recent FAR loop gave candidates the DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report and explored:

- Discussion areas: MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention), Aux-Loss-Free MoE, MTP (Multi-Token Prediction), and DualPipe.
- Repeated follow-ups: “What motivated this design?” and “How would you apply it in production?”

## Notes

- Prepare a seven-part structure that you can explain aloud: Problem → Key Idea → Architecture → Why These Choices → Evidence → Limitations → Production Translation.
- The interviewer is looking for judgments rather than recitation. Challenge the paper where appropriate—identify what remains unconvincing and propose the next experiment you would run.
- Keep the timing disciplined: 30 minutes on the paper supports three substantial topics, not ten superficial ones.
- A reusable seven-part critique sequence is: **Problem** (what gap exists and why it matters now) → **Key idea** (state it in one sentence) → **Architecture** (draw or describe a block diagram) → **Why these choices** (which alternatives the authors did not select) → **Evidence** (which result validates the main idea and which result is merely incidental) → **Limitations** (what is omitted and what scale remains untested) → **Production translation** (the latency, memory, and data expenses of operating it at your company).
- Interviewers value measured disagreement: choose an ablation you question or a missing baseline, then explain its significance. Saying, “I would compare this with X under the same compute budget,” is stronger than paraphrasing the abstract.
- For systems-oriented papers such as DeepSeek-V3, also be ready to discuss training compute, inference cost per token, memory on the serving side, and what would fail at 10× the scale.
- Allocate the time deliberately: 30 minutes of paper questions means three deep discussions rather than ten shallow ones. Decide which three you can defend before arriving.

## Preparation

- Use the 48 hours to make notes with the seven-part framework instead of rereading every line of the paper.
- For each major contribution, develop a production-translation perspective—Amazon especially rewards answers about operating systems at scale.
- Rehearse with a peer: explain the paper in five minutes, then take ten minutes of criticism.
- Practice in stages: (1) spend the first hour organizing notes with the seven-part framework rather than rereading line by line; (2) draw the architecture from memory—if you cannot, your understanding is not deep enough; (3) write one paragraph on production translation (“to serve this at 10k QPS, we would need…”); (4) rehearse with a peer, present for five minutes, take ten minutes of pushback, and revise.
- Create a general “why this design choice” template for each paper subsystem—attention variant, training objective, data mixture, and scaling law—and for every subsystem identify the rejected alternative plus one argument for and one against it.
- Commit one figure to memory for each major contribution, such as parameter count, training-token total, or throughput improvement; specific numbers show that you genuinely studied the paper.
- Strengthen the production-translation skill by choosing a recent paper you were not assigned and writing a one-page document titled “how would Amazon run this.” That capability carries directly into the interview.
